# Manage your Appside test store with an AI agent

> **Try it on your game, no signup:** paste your App Store or Google Play link at [appside.build/#preview](https://appside.build/?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=docs&utm_campaign=w45-preview&utm_content=docs-agent-store#preview) and see a draft store in seconds.

Appside's **publisher MCP adapter** lets a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or any MCP client) read and edit your store draft, configure offers and promo codes, confirm products and publish a test version, through the same checks the Studio applies. It runs on your machine, authenticates as your existing publisher account, and is **read-only unless you opt in to writes**.

This is a v0, local adapter for **TEST stores**. It is not a hosted connector, there are no scoped API tokens yet, and it never moves real money.

## Install from the download

```sh
mkdir appside-publisher-agent && cd appside-publisher-agent
curl -O https://appside.build/docs/downloads/publisher-mcp-0.1.0.tgz
curl -O https://appside.build/docs/downloads/publisher-mcp-0.1.0.tgz.sha256
shasum -a 256 -c publisher-mcp-0.1.0.tgz.sha256      # expect: OK
tar -xzf publisher-mcp-0.1.0.tgz                      # server.mjs, stdio.mjs, package.json, README.md
```

It's a plain archive, not an npm package, and it has no dependencies beyond Node 20+. Don't use `npx` with the package name.

## Configure your MCP client

Run `node /absolute/path/appside-publisher-agent/stdio.mjs` as a stdio server. Credentials go in the environment, never in tool arguments:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `APPSIDE_AGENT_EMAIL`, `APPSIDE_AGENT_PASSWORD` | An existing publisher account. Alternatively `APPSIDE_AGENT_SESSION`, an existing session token |
| `APPSIDE_AGENT_ORIGIN` | Defaults to `https://app.appside.build`. HTTPS is required except on loopback |
| `APPSIDE_AGENT_WRITES=1` | Opt in to draft edits, product confirmation and publishing. Default: read-only |

Example for a client that takes a JSON config:

```json
{"mcpServers":{"appside-publisher":{"command":"node","args":["/absolute/path/appside-publisher-agent/stdio.mjs"],"env":{"APPSIDE_AGENT_EMAIL":"you@studio.example","APPSIDE_AGENT_PASSWORD":"…"}}}}
```

## Tools

**Read (always available):** `get_agent_capabilities`, `list_games`, `get_store`, `get_analytics`, `get_checkout_link`.

**Write (with `APPSIDE_AGENT_WRITES=1`):** `set_theme_tokens`, `set_product`, `set_promo_code`, `set_section`, `set_banner`, `set_payment_methods`, `set_translation`, `confirm_product`, `publish_store`.

Setters take `{tenant, revision, value}` after a `get_store`. A product, promo code, section or banner value replaces one complete item; theme tokens and regional payment settings merge top-level keys. If the draft changed in the Studio since the agent read it, the call is refused with a revision conflict and nothing is overwritten: the agent re-reads and reapplies deliberately.

Two actions need an explicit confirmation string in the call, so an agent can't stumble into them: `confirm_product` needs `"confirmation":"PUBLISHER_APPROVED_PRODUCT"`, and `publish_store` needs `"confirmation":"PUBLISHER_APPROVED_PUBLICATION"` plus the expected `liveVersion`. Publishing also needs the owner role, and the server runs the same publish checks as the Studio (confirmed products, legal links, readable colours).

## What "personalization" means here

An offer can target a minimum player level, a spender tier, a country or new players. Those values come from the signed player attributes your backend puts in the player token. The adapter configures the rule; it doesn't guess a player profile or run a model.

## Checkout and analytics

`get_checkout_link` returns an existing published store link. Player sign-in, payment and delivery stay with the SDK, the checkout and your signed webhook: the agent can't spend on a player's behalf. `get_analytics` returns the backend's **test** aggregates (revenue in minor units for today and the last 7 days, refunds, top pack, funnel). They describe the test purchase flow, not visitors, attribution or production revenue.

## Verify the adapter

Without credentials, the server still answers `initialize` and lists the five read-only tools:

```sh
printf '%s\n%s\n' \
 '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-03-26","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"check","version":"0"}}}' \
 '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' | node stdio.mjs
```

Expected: server `appside-publisher-local` 0.1.0, then `get_agent_capabilities`, `list_games`, `get_store`, `get_analytics`, `get_checkout_link`.

## Security notes

- The adapter only talks to an exact HTTPS origin, refuses redirects, and times out after 15 seconds.
- The session cookie lives in process memory. Errors from the server are redacted before they reach the agent.
- Tool arguments are validated strictly; tenant IDs can't contain path segments.
- The adapter treats store text it reads as data, not instructions.
- Orders, audit rows, secrets, refunds, grants, team management, key rotation and AI generation are **not** exposed.

## Two different MCP connections

The public **https://appside.build/mcp** is read-only documentation for coding agents: it searches the docs, returns SDK examples and the published price, and needs no account. The publisher adapter on this page manages a store you own. Start with the [MCP docs page](/docs/mcp/) for the first, and this page for the second.

# The AI builder and Dex, the store advisor: what they do, and what they never do

Two AI features exist in Appside today. This page lists exactly what each one does, what it reads, and what it cannot touch. Both are disclosed as AI wherever they appear.

## The builder (`/build`)

**What it does.** You paste an App Store or Google Play link, or a name. A durable job (queued, leased, resumable) looks at the listing's icon and screenshots and drafts a store: theme (every text/background pair checked at 4.5:1 contrast or better), store name, currency name, product display names and images, hero and logo art. If the AI quota is exhausted, a measured-colour fallback drafts the theme from the icon without a model call.

**What it never changes.** Products' commerce fields (SKUs, credits, prices, bonuses), offers, promo codes, sections, the daily reward, legal links and membership plans always come from your existing draft. The builder's result is applied as a whole draft only if the draft has not changed since the job started, and it never publishes: publishing stays owner-only, through the publish checks.

**Cost caps.** A hard cap per run and a per-account quota. Pack art uses a paid image model only when a key is configured.

## Dex, the store advisor (Studio → Advisor)

**What it does today.** A read-only review of your saved draft and your own seven-day funnel. Ten deterministic rules, each with a stable id, a severity, the evidence it was computed from and a confidence:

| Rule id | Finding |
|---|---|
| `price-ladder-gap` | consecutive pack prices differ by more than 3× |
| `bonus-not-rising` | a higher-priced pack gives fewer credits per dollar than a cheaper one |
| `no-first-purchase-offer` | no offer enables first purchase |
| `empty-or-single-item-section` | a published section has at most one SKU |
| `contrast` | a theme text pair is below 4.5:1 |
| `legal-pages-missing` | terms or privacy links are missing |
| `plan-without-art-or-benefits` | a live plan has no image or fewer than two benefits |
| `daily-reward-off` | no enabled, confirmed daily reward |
| `stale-offers` | an offer's end date is in the past |
| `funnel-drop` | checkout → paid below 40% over seven days, only with at least 50 checkouts |

The review also lists its limitations every time: no model explanation yet, no economy or retention data, no in-app price list, no external benchmarks, and "not enough data yet" when a rule's minimum sample is not met.

**What it reads.** Your tenant's draft, its published sections, and its own funnel counts. Nothing from other publishers. Listing text and player data are treated as data, never as instructions.

**Proposals and apply (shipped).** A finding that has a fix carries a typed proposal. "Propose" stages it; the server computes the diff against the saved draft and shows it in the "Review changes" panel as before/after rows you can tick individually. "Apply selected" writes only the ticked rows, through the same revision check as a manual save, and records an `advisor.applied` entry in the audit log. Proposals are limited to an explicit allowlist: theme tokens, a product's display name, the order of sections, a plan's image, and a new offer added as an unconfirmed draft that copies an existing product's commerce (it cannot invent a price or entitlement). Anything else is refused with a 422.

**Dex on screen.** In Studio, Dex appears as a portrait with a state chip (idle, reviewing, found, warning, applied) and a disclosure line. Dex's portrait never moves on its own, never loops and never fades. In Studio it plays one short silent HeyGen clip, forward once, on a real event only (a review starting, a finding, a confirmed apply) and then holds its last frame. On the product page at `/advisor/` the same clips react to the sample review you start yourself, and one spoken tip plays in its own player only when you press the button, with captions. Every spoken line is bound to a rule id and says only what the product does today.

**What it never does.** Publish a version, confirm a price, change a published plan, read another tenant, or touch payment configuration. Dex is an original character and is labelled as an AI advisor wherever he appears.

## Planned (not available yet)

- A model-written explanation per finding, constrained to the evidence shown.
- More of Dex's reactions (today: reviewing, found, warning, applied) and a spoken explanation per finding, bound to the finding's evidence.
- Publisher-supplied economy inputs and an in-app price list import, each with its source.

This section is updated when each item ships; nothing above it is promised before it exists.

# Return to the game

After checkout, Appside sends the player back to your app through your **return URL**. The SDK turns that URL into a `PurchaseResult` you can show in the UI.

> The return is a **UI hint**. Grant items only from the [webhook](/docs/webhooks/) (or `getOrder` on your server). A player can close the browser before returning, and the webhook still arrives.

## Choose a return URL
- **Universal Link (iOS) / App Link (Android), recommended:** `https://yourgame.com/appside/return`. It works even when the app isn't installed. Studio → Integration generates the `apple-app-site-association` and `assetlinks.json` entries to host on your domain.
- **Custom scheme:** `orbitquest://appside`. Simplest to set up, but other apps could register the same scheme.

## Handle it
- iOS: `Appside.handle(url)` in `scene(_:openURLContexts:)` or SwiftUI `.onOpenURL`.
- Android: `Appside.handle(intent.data)` in the activity with the matching `<intent-filter>`.
- Unity: the SDK registers the handler. Subscribe to `Appside.OnPurchaseCompleted`.
- Web: the store returns to `returnURL` with `?appside_order=…`, and `Appside.handle(location.href)` reads it.

## Result fields
`status` (`completed` · `canceled` · `failed`), `orderId`, `sku`, `credits`, `error` (for failures).

# Sell from your game's own web store

Appside is a web store builder for games. It gives your game a web store that looks and feels like your app, a checkout, and delivery of purchased items back into your game. Players move from the app to the store **already signed in**, pay, and their items land in the game in seconds.

> **Status:** test mode. Every flow on these pages works end to end against the Appside sandbox. Live payments are on the roadmap. Each SDK page says whether it is **built and tested** or **preview source**.

## Three steps, on every platform

| | What you build | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Sign a player token**: a 5-minute ES256 JWT that says who the player is | your game backend |
| 2 | **Open the store or a pack**: `Appside.openStore(token)` or `Appside.purchase("voyager", token)` | your app or game client |
| 3 | **Grant on the webhook**: verify `order.paid` and credit the player once per `order_id` | your game backend |

There is no server-to-server checkout session to create and no separate store-login system to run. The price always comes from the catalogue you published in Studio, so a client can't tamper with it.

```mermaid-ish
Game client ──openStore(token)──▶ Appside store ──pay──▶ Appside
     ▲                                                    │
     └── returnURL (deep link, UI hint only)              │ order.paid (signed webhook)
                                                          ▼
                                                   Your game backend ──grants items
```

- [Player tokens](/docs/player-tokens/)
- [Webhooks: order.paid and order.refunded](/docs/webhooks/)
- [Return to the game: deep links and universal links](/docs/deep-links/)

# Appside MCP: game web store docs for your coding agent

Appside's public MCP server lets compatible coding agents search developer documentation, retrieve SDK examples and read published pricing. Its three tools are read-only: they do not create stores, publish sites or process payments.

## Connect your coding agent

Use **https://appside.build/mcp** with a client that supports remote Streamable HTTP. No account, API key or payment credentials are required. For clients supporting this URL configuration:

```json
{"mcpServers":{"appside":{"url":"https://appside.build/mcp"}}}
```

Configuration fields vary by client. Choose its remote HTTP connector, rather than a local executable or SSE-only connection. See the [MCP remote connection guide](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-remote-servers).

## Available tools

| Tool | Arguments | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `search_docs` | `query`: 1–200 characters | Up to five documentation excerpts with source links |
| `get_sdk_snippet` | `platform`: one of the names below | SDK README examples and documented verification status |
| `get_pricing` | An empty object | Published fee, fee basis and source URL |

Supported platform names: `web`, `ios`, `android`, `unity`, `react-native`, `flutter`, `node`, `python`. Available examples do not mean every platform has been tested on a device: check the returned status and [SDK verification details](/docs/sdks/).

The server also exposes **https://appside.build/llms.txt** as a read-only MCP resource. For clients without MCP, use [the documentation index](/llms.txt), [full developer text](/llms-full.txt) or this page's **View as Markdown** link.

## Try a useful integration prompt

Ask your agent: “Search Appside's docs for signed webhooks, get the Node SDK example, and explain how my backend grants each order only once. Include source links and identify any test-mode limitations.”

Expected sequence: `search_docs` with `{"query":"signed webhooks"}`, followed by `get_sdk_snippet` with `{"platform":"node"}`. Read the linked [webhook guide](/docs/webhooks/) before integrating. A return-to-game link or client callback is a UI hint; grant items only after verified backend delivery.

## Verify the connection

The endpoint speaks protocol **2025-03-26**. This initialization request can be run without credentials:

```sh
curl https://appside.build/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-03-26","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"docs-check","version":"1.0.0"}}}'
```

A public endpoint check on **2026-10-24 UTC** returned server name `appside-mcp`, version `0.1.0`, all three tools above, and a successful `get_pricing` response. You can reproduce the pricing call:

```sh
curl https://appside.build/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_pricing","arguments":{}}}'
```

The text content contains `feePercent: 3.9`, `basis: "per successful payment"`, and zero setup, subscription and minimum fees, with a source link. This is published pricing information, not a payment-processing tool or confirmation that a merchant is approved for live payments. See [testing and payment status](/docs/testing/).

## Limits and troubleshooting

- Stateless JSON POST responses; notification POSTs return an empty 202. GET returns 405: there is no optional SSE stream, session state or server-initiated messaging.
- Set both headers shown above. Missing JSON content type returns 415; missing accepted response types returns 406.
- Limits: 64 KiB messages, 20-message batches, 10s body deadline, 60 requests/minute per socket IP and 600/minute globally. Behind the edge proxy, clients may share a socket bucket.
- A 429 response includes `Retry-After: 60`. Wait before retrying instead of polling repeatedly.
- There is no cross-origin browser CORS access. If an Origin header is present, it must match an allowed HTTPS site origin. Connect from your MCP client's server-side transport.

## Managing a store you own

This public endpoint reads documentation; it can't change a store. To let your agent edit a draft, configure offers and publish a test version of a store you own, use the local **publisher MCP adapter**: a downloadable, read-only-by-default stdio server that authenticates as your publisher account. See [Manage your store with an AI agent](/docs/agent-store/).

## Discovery and next steps

Find the public [Appside Developer Docs listing on Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/connectors/build.appside/appside-developer-docs). The listing is live; the ownership claim is pending. The official MCP registry entry and npm package are not published, so use the remote endpoint above.

Start with the [first-purchase quickstart](/docs/quickstart/), connect [player identity](/docs/player-tokens/), then implement [signed fulfillment](/docs/webhooks/). Publishers with an Appside account create and manage the store in the [Appside builder](https://app.appside.build/build); to see the app-to-store journey first, open the [live demo](https://demo.appside.build/demo).

---
title: 'How to migrate from Appcharge to Appside: Payment Links to player tokens and signed webhooks'
nav: From Appcharge
order: 8
---
# Coming from Appcharge Payment Links

To migrate from Appcharge to Appside, adapt your existing item-granting logic to verified `order.paid` events, add a backend endpoint that signs player tokens, and replace the client checkout call. Recreate and confirm your catalogue in Appside before routing players to it. The examples below use test mode so you can verify the complete purchase and delivery path before switching traffic.

## The migration in seven steps

1. **Audit what you use.** Web store, Checkout API, mobile checkout SDK, subscriptions; how items are granted today and how refunds are handled.
2. **Export your data.** Transaction history, player-to-customer mappings, the product catalogue, subscription records and financial reports. Appcharge's public documentation does not describe a self-service migration-away procedure (checked October 29, 2026), so ask its support for export rights and offboarding terms in writing.
3. **Set up Appside.** [Create your store](https://app.appside.build/signup), paste your app link, confirm every SKU, price, currency, bonus and bundle against the export. Nothing here imports an Appcharge catalogue automatically.
4. **Update your backend and client**: the three sections below (player tokens, the granting endpoint, the checkout call) and the return path.
5. **Handle subscriptions.** Card tokens do not move between providers. Keep existing Appcharge subscriptions running to their paid dates and offer the Appside pass to those players; new memberships start on Appside ([subscriptions](/docs/subscriptions/)).
6. **Run both during the switch.** Route new purchases to Appside while Appcharge stays live for historical purchases, refunds and open disputes; namespace records by provider.
7. **Reconcile and offboard.** Settlements, chargebacks, tax reports and subscription renewals verified on both sides before the Appcharge agreement ends. The [switching checklist](/switching-web-store-providers-checklist/) has the 20 items.

## Map your existing integration

Appcharge references checked **October 25, 2026**. These are integration concepts, not interchangeable payloads or credentials.

| Existing Appcharge integration | Appside implementation |
|---|---|
| [Create Checkout Session](https://docs.appcharge.com/api-reference/checkout/checkout-session/create-checkout-session) sends offer, customer and price details to create a session. | Sign a short-lived player token on your backend; call `purchase(sku, token)` for a SKU in your published catalogue. |
| [Authenticate Player Callback](https://docs.appcharge.com/api-reference/webstore/player-authentication/authenticate-player-callback) authenticates a web-store player through your server. | Your authenticated backend signs the player identity into a single-use ES256 token. See [player tokens](/docs/player-tokens/). |
| [Grant Award Callback](https://docs.appcharge.com/api-reference/checkout/awards/grant-award-callback) sends award details to your endpoint. | Verify the Appside webhook, map its payload into your granting logic, and handle `order.paid` and `order.refunded` separately. |

Keep existing player IDs stable. Map every source product to an Appside SKU and check currency, price, credits, bundles and bonuses. This guide does not import an Appcharge catalogue or historical orders automatically.

## 1. Add an authenticated player-token endpoint

Install the Node SDK from [SDK downloads](/docs/sdks/). In Studio → Integration, configure your issuer and upload the public JWK matching your backend signing key. Keep the private key on your server. This is the Node example from the [quickstart](/docs/quickstart/):

```js
import { Appside } from '@appside/server';
const appside = new Appside({ storeId: 'orbit', issuer: 'orbit', kid: 'game-key-1',
  privateKey: process.env.APPSIDE_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM, webhookSecret: process.env.APPSIDE_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
  serverKey: process.env.APPSIDE_SERVER_KEY, baseURL: 'https://app.appside.build' });

app.post('/appside/token', requireLogin, (req, res) =>
  res.json({ token: appside.playerToken(req.user.id) }));
```

`app` and `requireLogin` belong to your existing server. Authenticate the session before signing; never accept an arbitrary player ID from the client. Request a fresh token each time you open the store. Tokens expire within five minutes and cannot be reused.

## 2. Adapt your granting endpoint

Set your Fulfillment URL and a webhook secret of at least 32 characters in Studio. Register the raw-body route before any JSON middleware that consumes its body. The [webhook reference](/docs/webhooks/) specifies HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp followed by a period and the original request bytes, using `x-appside-timestamp` and `x-appside-signature`. Reject timestamps outside the 300-second window.

```js
app.post('/appside/webhook', express.raw({ type: '*/*' }), async (req, res) => {
  if (!appside.verifyWebhook(req.body, req.headers)) return res.sendStatus(401);
  const event = JSON.parse(req.body);
  if (event.type === 'order.paid' && !event.probe) await grantOnce(event.order_id, event.player_id, event.order);
  if (event.type === 'order.refunded') await revokeOnce(event.order_id, event.player_id);
  res.sendStatus(204);
});
```

This excerpt uses your Express server and your own `grantOnce` and `revokeOnce` implementations. Persist deduplication and the wallet update in the same database transaction. Namespace records by provider and event type so a refund is not mistaken for a duplicate purchase. Acknowledge only after the transaction commits. Appside retries unsuccessful deliveries for up to 72 hours. A probe is acknowledged without granting items.

Do not copy Appcharge signature validation into this route: the providers use different headers and payloads. Do not grant from a browser redirect or SDK completion callback.

## 3. Replace the client checkout call

Use a fresh token with the SKU configured in Appside. This Web example follows the quickstart:

```js
import { Appside } from 'appside/web';
const appside = new Appside({ baseURL: 'https://app.appside.build' });
appside.configure('orbit', { environment: 'test', returnURL: 'https://yourgame.com/appside/return' });
const fresh = () => fetch('/appside/token', { method: 'POST' }).then(r => r.json()).then(j => j.token);
await appside.purchase('voyager', await fresh());
```

For the whole store, use `openStore(await fresh())` instead. On the return page, call `appside.handle(location.href)` and refresh the balance from your backend. The return result is a UI hint, not proof that items were granted.

Use the platform-specific examples and current verification status in [SDK downloads](/docs/sdks/). For coding assistants, the [Appside MCP guide](/docs/mcp/) provides another way to discover the integration documentation.

## 4. Configure the return path

Set the return URL in Studio and your SDK. For Universal Links and Android App Links, Studio generates association entries; you still need to host the relevant AASA or assetlinks file on your domain and configure the app. Follow [Return to the game](/docs/deep-links/) and test both an installed-app return and a closed browser.

## 5. Prove the flow before routing players

- Publish a test catalogue with confirmed SKUs and prices.
- Send a Studio test event and verify acknowledgment without a balance change.
- Complete a simulated purchase, a decline and a refund using [Testing](/docs/testing/).
- Deliver a duplicate event and verify that the player receives items only once.
- Simulate an unavailable receiver, then verify retry and acknowledgment in Integration and Orders.

[Download the webhook proof kit](/docs/downloads/appside-webhook-proof.mjs) and run it with Node 20 or later:

```sh
node appside-webhook-proof.mjs
```

Its six local checks cover a valid purchase, duplicate delivery, changed body, expired timestamp, wrong secret and refund replay. It uses an in-memory wallet; use durable storage in your receiver. Passing it does not verify a hosted endpoint or live payment activation.

## Run both providers during the switch

A gradual rollout is an application-side approach: use your own feature flag to route a cohort to Appside while existing players continue through Appcharge. Keep separate verification adapters feeding your shared granting service. Retain provider-specific event IDs, refund handling and reconciliation until old orders and retries are resolved. Do not send the same purchase to both providers.

## Check the costs

Appside's published price is **3.9% per successful payment**, with no setup fee, subscription or minimum. Use the [fee calculator](/tools/app-store-fee-calculator/) with your own assumptions and the sourced [Appside vs Appcharge comparison](/appcharge-alternative/) for context. Confirm commercial terms and activation requirements before moving production traffic.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need to rewrite my item-granting code?

You can retain its business logic. Add an adapter for Appside's verified payload, durable deduplication and refund handling. Test the SKU and entitlement mapping before routing traffic.

### Can I keep Appcharge running during migration?

Yes, you can route players using a flag in your own application. Maintain both webhook receivers and provider-specific reconciliation. Appside does not manage that traffic flag for you.

### How do players log in without an Authenticate Player Callback?

Your authenticated backend signs a fresh, single-use player token. Appside verifies it against the public keys you configured in Studio. Never sign tokens in the mobile app or browser.

### Which SDK should I use?

Choose your platform in [SDK downloads](/docs/sdks/) and check its current verification status. The [quickstart](/docs/quickstart/) has examples for Web, iOS, Android, Unity, React Native and Flutter.

### Does a successful return URL mean I should grant items?

No. Grant only after server-side verification. A player can close the browser before returning, and a browser callback can be forged. Use the signed webhook and refresh the UI from your backend.

### Is there a setup fee?

Appside's published pricing has no setup fee, subscription or minimum. The rate is 3.9% per successful payment.

[Create your Appside workspace](https://app.appside.build/signup) and follow the [quickstart](/docs/quickstart/) to test your first mapped product.

# Player data: show the player their balance, level and name in the store

The store opens signed in from a [player token](/docs/player-tokens/). To show the player who they are (name, avatar, level, currency balances) and to refresh those after a purchase and after a free reward is claimed, your backend exposes one read-only endpoint that the store calls. It is optional: without it the store shows the level from the token, and no balances. The spender tier is never shown to the player.

## The endpoint

Register the URL in Studio → Integration → **Player data URL** (HTTPS, your domain). The store calls:

```
GET <playerDataUrl>?player=<player_id>
x-appside-timestamp: 1793268000
x-appside-signature: <lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256>
Accept: application/json
```

The store calls with two headers, the same scheme as webhooks:

- `x-appside-timestamp`: Unix time in **seconds** (integer, as a decimal string).
- `x-appside-signature`: **lowercase hex** HMAC-SHA256, keyed with your store's webhook secret, over the UTF-8 string `"<timestamp>.player-data.<player_id>"`, where `<player_id>` is exactly the `player` query value.

Verify with a constant-time comparison, and reject timestamps more than 300 seconds from your clock. There is no `Authorization` header. The `player-data.` prefix keeps these signatures apart from webhook signatures made with the same secret: a webhook signature covers `"<ts>." + rawBody`, and a JSON body never starts with `player-data.`.

## The response

```json
{
  "name": "Wisp",
  "avatar": "https://game.example/avatars/wisp.png",
  "level": 12,
  "balances": [
    { "currency": "shards", "label": "Star Shards", "amount": 550, "icon": "https://game.example/icons/shard.png" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Shown |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤ 40 | Header |
| `avatar` | HTTPS image URL | Header |
| `level` | integer 0–1,000,000 | Header only |
| `balances[]` | up to 4 currencies (`currency`, `label`, `amount`, `icon`) | Header; the first is the primary balance |

Offer targeting uses only the attributes in the signed player token (level, spender tier, country, new player). Data returned by this endpoint is displayed and never changes which offers a player can buy. `tier` and `segments` fields, if present, are ignored.

Every field is optional. Unknown fields are ignored. The response must be `application/json`, under 8 KB, and answer within 2 seconds; on error or timeout the store falls back to the token attributes and shows no balances.

## When the store calls it

- When the store opens (after the player token is verified).
- After your backend acknowledges `order.paid` (a 2xx response to the signed webhook). Until then the store shows "Delivering…". The balance shown is whatever this endpoint returns; the store never computes balances itself, and showing a balance is not confirmation of a payment or a grant.
- At most once per 60 seconds per player otherwise (cached).

## Security notes

- Return data only for the `player` in the query, and only after verifying the signature.
- Never include secrets, emails or payment details.
- The endpoint is read-only: nothing the store sends changes the wallet. Grants happen only through your signed webhook handler.

## Example (Node)

```js
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';

function verifyPlayerDataSignature(req, secret) {
  const ts = String(req.get('x-appside-timestamp') || ''), sig = String(req.get('x-appside-signature') || '');
  if (!/^\d+$/.test(ts) || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(ts)) > 300) return false;
  const expected = createHmac('sha256', secret).update(`${ts}.player-data.${req.query.player}`).digest();
  const given = Buffer.from(sig, 'hex');
  return given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(given, expected);
}

app.get('/appside/player', async (req, res) => {
  if (!verifyPlayerDataSignature(req, process.env.APPSIDE_WEBHOOK_SECRET)) return res.status(401).end();
  const p = await players.get(req.query.player);
  if (!p) return res.status(404).end();
  res.json({ name: p.displayName, avatar: p.avatarUrl, level: p.level,
    balances: [{ currency: 'shards', label: 'Star Shards', amount: p.shards }] });
});
```

# Player tokens

A player token is how your game tells Appside who is buying, **without** a login screen and without Appside calling your server to authenticate. It's a compact JWS (JWT) signed by your backend with ES256 (P-256).

## Claims (all required unless marked)
| Claim | Value |
|---|---|
| `alg` (header) | `ES256` |
| `kid` (header) | id of a public key you uploaded in Studio → Integration |
| `iss` | your issuer string, exactly as configured |
| `aud` | `appside:store:<storeId>` |
| `tenant` | your store id |
| `player_id` | your stable player id (≤ 200 chars) |
| `nonce` | 16–128 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, unique per token |
| `exp` | ≤ 5 minutes after now |
| `iat`, `nbf` | optional |
| `attributes` | optional object of trusted player targeting attributes (below) |

## Rules Appside enforces
- **Single use:** the nonce is consumed atomically. Opening the same token twice fails with *Player assertion already used*.
- **Short-lived:** anything over 5 minutes is rejected.
- **Your keys only:** Appside accepts public JWKs only. Uploading a private key is refused.
- **Rotation:** upload the new public key next to the old one, switch your backend to the new `kid`, wait 5 minutes, then remove the old key.

## Never in the client
Signing keys stay on your backend. The app asks your backend for a fresh token each time it opens the store.

## Targeted offers

Node and Python server SDKs 0.1.1 accept an optional second argument to `playerToken`. Read these values from your authenticated player record on your backend; never trust attributes supplied by the client. They are signed into the `attributes` claim and used to match targeted offers.

| Attribute | Accepted value |
|---|---|
| `level` | Integer from 0 to 1,000,000 inclusive |
| `spenderTier` | `none`, `low`, `medium`, or `high` |
| `country` | Two uppercase ASCII letters, such as `US` (ISO-2 format; no country-directory lookup) |
| `newPlayer` | Boolean |

Every field is optional. Invalid recognized values throw before signing; unknown fields are discarded. Omitting the argument preserves the existing token without an `attributes` claim. An empty object is allowed. A targeted offer requires every configured field to match; level means the player's level is at least the configured threshold. Missing fields do not match that target.

### Node
```js
import { Appside } from '@appside/server';
const appside = new Appside({
  storeId: 'my-store', kid: 'key-1', privateKey: process.env.APPSIDE_PRIVATE_KEY
});
const token = appside.playerToken('player-123', {
  level: 12, spenderTier: 'low', country: 'US', newPlayer: false
});
```

### Python
```python
import os
from appside import Appside
appside = Appside('my-store', kid='key-1', privateKey=os.environ['APPSIDE_PRIVATE_KEY'])
token = appside.playerToken('player-123', {
    'level': 12, 'spenderTier': 'low', 'country': 'US', 'newPlayer': False
})
```

# Subscriptions: a membership or season pass sold on the web, renewed by card

> **Available.** Memberships run on any store that publishes a plan in Studio → Catalogue → Plans. Cards, prices in USD, EUR and GBP. Free trials and resuming a cancelled membership are not in this version; see Limits.

A subscription is a plan the player buys in your web store and that renews automatically: a monthly VIP membership, a season pass, a "shard stipend" that drops currency every month. Appside charges the card each cycle and tells your backend what happened. **Your backend owns the entitlement**: it grants on `subscription.started`, keeps granting on `subscription.renewed`, and revokes on `subscription.expired`. The store never changes a wallet or a flag itself.

## Plans

A plan is created in Studio → Catalogue → **Plans**:

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `plan_id` | your key, `[a-z0-9-]{2,40}`, stable once published |
| `name` | shown on the card and the receipt |
| `period` | `month` or `year` |
| `prices` | one price per currency: USD, EUR and GBP in v1; the player pays in the currency the store shows them, and the subscription keeps that currency |
| `trial_days` | `0` to `30`; the card is stored at sign-up and first charged when the trial ends |
| `benefits[]` | up to 6 lines shown on the card; text only, the game decides what they mean |
| `state` | `draft`, `live`, `paused` (no new subscribers), `retired` (existing run to period end) |

A store can have several plans. Switching between plans (upgrade, downgrade, proration) is not in v1: a player cancels one and subscribes to another.

## Events to your Fulfillment URL

Every change is delivered to the same **Fulfillment URL** as orders, as a signed HTTPS POST with the same headers, signature, retries and dedupe rules as [`order.paid`](/docs/webhooks/). Acknowledge with 2xx; dedupe on `idempotency-key`.

```json
{
  "type": "subscription.renewed",
  "event_id": "SUB-9a2f…:3",
  "mode": "test",
  "tenant": "orbit",
  "player_id": "player-123",
  "probe": false,
  "subscription": {
    "id": "SUB-9a2f…",
    "plan_id": "star-pass",
    "status": "active",
    "cycle": 3,
    "period_start": "2026-01-15T10:00:00Z",
    "period_end": "2026-02-15T10:00:00Z",
    "price": 499,
    "currency": "USD",
    "cancel_at_period_end": false
  }
}
```

| Event | When | What your backend does |
|---|---|---|
| `subscription.started` | first charge paid, or trial began (`cycle` 1; `price` 0 during a trial) | grant the benefits until `period_end` |
| `subscription.renewed` | a renewal charge paid | extend the benefits to the new `period_end` |
| `subscription.payment_failed` | a renewal charge failed; `grace_until` is set | keep the benefits until `grace_until`; optionally tell the player in-game |
| `subscription.canceled` | the player canceled; `cancel_at_period_end` is `true` | nothing yet; benefits run to `period_end` |
| `subscription.expired` | `period_end` or `grace_until` passed without a paid cycle | revoke the benefits |
| `subscription.refunded` | a cycle was refunded from Studio; `refunded_cycle` is set | your decision: usually revoke for that cycle |

`event_id` is `<subscription_id>:<cycle>` for `started` and `renewed`, and `<subscription_id>:<cycle>:<event>` for the others, so each is granted or revoked exactly once. Events for one subscription arrive in order; if your backend is down, retries keep the order. `probe: true` is the Studio **Send test event**: acknowledge it, grant nothing.

`price` is in minor units (cents) like `order.price`. `status` is one of `trialing`, `active`, `past_due`, `canceled`, `expired`.

## What the player sees

- A **Membership** card in the store with the plan, the price per period, the benefits and, if any, the trial. Checkout is the same checkout as a pack: card, saved for renewals, with the renewal terms shown before the player confirms.
- In the player area: the plan, the next charge date and amount, the payment history, and **Cancel**, one tap, effective at period end, no questions asked. Cancelling is final for that subscription: the membership runs to the paid date, and the player can subscribe again afterwards.
- After a failed renewal: a "payment failed, update your card" notice with a retry; no benefits are removed until `grace_until`.

Access is tied to the `player_id` in the [player token](/docs/player-tokens/). If the same player also holds an in-app subscription, that is your union to compute; the store knows only about the web plan.

## Limits and rules

- Cards only in v1. Direct Debit, wallets and other methods come later.
- Plan prices in USD, EUR and GBP in v1; a subscription keeps the currency it started in. Other currencies later.
- Trials: a plan can be drafted with `trial_days`, but publishing a live plan with a trial is blocked in this version.
- Resume: not available before the paid period ends; the player subscribes again afterwards (a new subscription).
- Grace after a failed renewal: 7 days with retries on days 1, 3 and 5; then `subscription.expired`.
- Refunds are per cycle from Studio and send `subscription.refunded`.
- Taxes and the merchant of record are yours, as everywhere in Appside.
- Rate: the published per-payment rate, applied to each paid cycle. Nothing per plan or per subscriber.

## Test mode

Plans and subscriptions work in test mode with the test card from the [testing](/docs/testing/) page (Google Pay in the sandbox works too). Renewals follow the real monthly or annual cycle; `payment_failed` and `expired` are produced by the provider's retry cycle, so plan a full cycle for an end-to-end test of those.

## Example (Node)

```js
app.post('/appside/fulfillment', verifyAppside, async (req, res) => {
  const ev = req.body;
  if (ev.probe) return res.sendStatus(200);
  if (await seen(ev.event_id)) return res.sendStatus(200);
  const s = ev.subscription;
  switch (ev.type) {
    case 'subscription.started':
    case 'subscription.renewed':
      await grantPass(ev.player_id, s.plan_id, new Date(s.period_end)); break;
    case 'subscription.payment_failed':
      await grantPass(ev.player_id, s.plan_id, new Date(s.grace_until)); break;
    case 'subscription.expired':
    case 'subscription.refunded':
      await revokePass(ev.player_id, s.plan_id); break;
    case 'subscription.canceled':
      break; // runs to period_end; nothing to do yet
    default:
      return handleOrderEvent(ev, res);
  }
  await markSeen(ev.event_id);
  res.sendStatus(200);
});
```

# Testing

Everything runs in **test mode**: no real money moves and your backend must keep test orders separate from production entitlements.

## Test cards
| Card | Result |
|---|---|
| `4242 4242 4242 4242` | Approved |
| `4000 0000 0000 0002` | Declined: balance unchanged |
| `4000 0027 6000 3184` | 3-D Secure challenge, then approved after **Authenticate** |

Any future expiry and any 3-digit CVC. Real card numbers are rejected on the client and the server, and full card numbers are never stored.

**Apple Pay / Google Pay:** simulated buttons in test mode.

## Checks worth automating
1. A purchase credits your player once (watch your `order_id` dedupe).
2. A declined card leaves the balance unchanged.
3. A replayed player token is refused.
4. **Outage:** stop your webhook endpoint, buy, start it again. The coins arrive after it comes back, exactly once.
5. **Refund** from Studio → Orders: your backend gets `order.refunded`, so revoke (never below zero).

Studio → Integration → **Send test event** sends a `probe` webhook that grants nothing.

title: Webhooks
nav: Webhooks
order: 4
---
# Webhooks: `order.paid` and `order.refunded`

Appside delivers every paid and refunded order to your **Fulfillment URL** as a signed HTTPS POST. This is the only place you should grant or revoke items.

## Payload
```json
{
  "type": "order.paid",
  "event_id": "TEST-6f1c…",
  "mode": "test",
  "tenant": "orbit",
  "order_id": "TEST-6f1c…",
  "player_id": "player-123",
  "probe": false,
  "order": { "id": "TEST-6f1c…", "sku": "voyager", "credits": 1400, "price": 799, "currency": "USD", "version": 3 }
}
```
- `order.refunded` carries the same `order_id`; its `event_id` is `<order_id>:refund`.
- `probe: true` is the Studio **Send test event**: acknowledge it, grant nothing.

## Headers
| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x-appside-timestamp` | Unix seconds when signed |
| `x-appside-signature` | hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"<timestamp>." + rawBody` with your webhook secret |
| `idempotency-key` | the `event_id`; dedupe on it |

## Verify the signature
Reject if the timestamp is more than 5 minutes off, then compare in constant time.

:::tabs
```js Node
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';
export function verify(raw, h, secret) {
  const ts = h['x-appside-timestamp'], sig = h['x-appside-signature'] || '';
  if (!/^\d{10}$/.test(ts) || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - ts) > 300) return false;
  const want = createHmac('sha256', secret).update(`${ts}.`).update(raw).digest();
  const got = Buffer.from(sig, 'hex');
  return got.length === want.length && timingSafeEqual(got, want);
}
```
```python Python
import hmac, hashlib, time
def verify(raw: bytes, h, secret: str) -> bool:
    ts, sig = h.get("x-appside-timestamp", ""), h.get("x-appside-signature", "")
    if not ts.isdigit() or abs(time.time() - int(ts)) > 300: return False
    want = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{ts}.".encode() + raw, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(want, sig)
```
```go Go
func Verify(raw []byte, ts, sig, secret string) bool {
  t, err := strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
  if err != nil || math.Abs(float64(time.Now().Unix()-t)) > 300 { return false }
  m := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret)); m.Write([]byte(ts + ".")); m.Write(raw)
  return hmac.Equal([]byte(hex.EncodeToString(m.Sum(nil))), []byte(sig))
}
```
```csharp C#
static bool Verify(byte[] raw, string ts, string sig, string secret) {
  if (!long.TryParse(ts, out var t) || Math.Abs(DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds() - t) > 300) return false;
  using var h = new HMACSHA256(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(secret));
  var want = Convert.ToHexString(h.ComputeHash(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(ts + ".").Concat(raw).ToArray())).ToLowerInvariant();
  return CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(want), Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(sig));
}
```
:::

## Verify it yourself

[Download the standalone webhook proof](/docs/downloads/appside-webhook-proof.mjs), save it as `appside-webhook-proof.mjs`, and run it with Node 20 or later. No packages, account or API key are needed.

```sh
node appside-webhook-proof.mjs
```

The six checks cover a valid purchase, duplicate delivery, a changed body, an expired timestamp, a wrong signing secret and a refund with replay. The balance moves from **0 to 125**, stays at **125** through the duplicate and rejected requests, then returns to **0** after the refund. Every case prints `"passed": true`; a failure exits with a nonzero code.

The exported `verifyAppsideWebhook({headers, rawBody, secret, now})` function implements the same signature check as the snippets above. `now` defaults to the current time in milliseconds; pass the original request bytes as `rawBody`.

This is a local reference receiver, not a hosted delivery or live payment test. Its wallet is in memory; a production receiver needs durable storage and an atomic transaction for deduplication and balance updates. Refunds revoke at most the remaining balance.

## Delivery guarantees
- The order and its webhook are written in **one transaction**: a paid order is never left without a delivery.
- Retries with exponential backoff (1 s, capped at 1 h) for **72 hours**. Only `2xx` counts as delivered, and redirects are not followed.
- Your endpoint can be down and come back: deliveries resume, and your `order_id` dedupe makes them land exactly once in your game.
- Studio → **Integration → Health** shows the last acknowledgement, failures in the last 24 h, and dead letters.

## `reward.claimed`: free rewards, granted the same way

When your store offers a free reward (a daily bonus, a reward-calendar day, a progress-bar milestone), the claim is delivered to your Fulfillment URL as a signed POST with the same headers, signature, retries and dedupe rules as `order.paid`. Grant exactly once per `reward_id`; the store never changes a wallet itself.

```json
{
  "type": "reward.claimed",
  "event_id": "RWD-3b2a…",
  "mode": "test",
  "tenant": "orbit",
  "reward_id": "RWD-3b2a…",
  "player_id": "player-123",
  "reward": { "kind": "daily_bonus", "credits": 25, "day": "2026-11-03", "calendar_day": null, "milestone": null }
}
```

- `kind` is `daily_bonus`, `calendar` (with `calendar_day` 1–30) or `progress` (with `milestone`).
- The store enforces the limits you set (one daily bonus per player per UTC day, one claim per calendar day, each milestone once) before sending; your handler should still key on `reward_id`.
- `probe: true` behaves as for orders: acknowledge, grant nothing.
- After a 2xx, the store will refresh the player header through the [player data endpoint](/docs/player-data/) once both ship.

# Android · Kotlin Appside

**Built and JVM-tested (2026-10-24).** Android library; debug and release AARs produced. Package intention: `build.appside:sdk`; not published. Device/app-link integration is not yet tested.

```kotlin
val appside = Appside(activity, "https://your-studio-host")
appside.configure("orbit", "test", "orbit://return")
appside.openStore(playerToken)
appside.purchase("voyager", freshPlayerToken)
val result = appside.handle(intent.data.toString())
```

Launch methods return CompletableFuture<Uri>. HTTP runs in a background executor; Custom Tabs opens on the main thread. Call `handle` from onNewIntent/onCreate with your registered intent filter, on the main thread. Requires AndroidX Browser, API 24+. A Custom Tab dismissal does not imply cancellation; host lifecycle may call its own closed UI handler. `onStoreClosed` is emitted for explicit `status=closed` returns. Compile and run device/link tests before shipping.

# Python server SDK

Install from this directory (`python -m pip install ./sdks/python`). Requires cryptography. Tests executed: `PYTHONPATH=sdks/python python3 -m unittest discover -s sdks/python`. Backend only.

```python
from appside import Appside
appside = Appside('orbit', issuer='orbit', kid='key-1', privateKey=pem,
    webhookSecret=secret, serverKey=server_key, baseURL='https://your-studio-host')
token = appside.playerToken(authenticated_player_id)
valid = appside.verifyWebhook(raw_body_bytes, headers)
order = appside.getOrder(order_id)
```

Names intentionally match Node/client SDK spelling. `playerToken` returns a five-minute ES256 JWS; `verifyWebhook` returns boolean over exact bytes with timestamp tolerance; `getOrder` is synchronous and raises on HTTP failures (10-second timeout). Use an authenticated backend player identity. Validate event fields, mode and tenant, then dedupe before granting.

Since 0.1.1, `playerToken(playerId, attributes)` optionally signs trusted backend targeting data: `level` (integer 0–1,000,000), `spenderTier` (`none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`), `country` (two uppercase ASCII letters), and `newPlayer` (boolean). All fields are optional; invalid values throw and unknown fields are discarded. Omitting attributes keeps the existing token format. See https://appside.build/docs/player-tokens/ for examples.
